key_insight: HTP-Net improves instance segmentation of dense, slender welding material stubs by preserving boundaries, modeling long-range topology, and using orientation-aware predictions.
engineering_relevance: More reliable stub counting and shape measurement can support automated inventory management in welding factories.
method: Wavelet-driven edge preservation retains subtle boundaries during feature downsampling.
Long-range topology modeling reduces fragmentation of slender targets.
Orientation-driven segmentation uses rotational priors to reduce excessive suppression and overlapping masks.
evidence_signal: On custom and public datasets, the abstract reports mAP50 gains of 1.2%–55.3% over existing methods; factory validation achieved average recognition accuracies of 99% for electrode stubs and 94% for wire stubs.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, inference speed, or robustness across factory imaging conditions, leaving deployment generalizability uncertain.
paper_title: High-resolution topology-preserving instance segmentation network for vision-based measurement system of dense welding material stubs
